stem.text: Two boxes X and Y have the same mass. Box X is lifted vertically through a height $h$ by a force of magnitude $F$.
Box Y is pulled along a slope by a force of the same magnitude to reach the same height, as shown.

stem.alt: Box X, a square block lifted by a vertical force labelled F, with a vertical dimension h between dashed markers; labelled box X.
Box Y, a block on a slope rising to the right, pulled up the slope by a force labelled F; a vertical dimension h between dashed markers at the top of the slope; labelled box Y.

A.text: Both boxes gain the same amount of gravitational potential energy and the same amount of work is done by the two forces.

B.text: Both boxes gain the same amount of gravitational potential energy but more work is done by the force acting on box Y than by the force acting on box X.

C.text: Box Y gains less gravitational potential energy than box X because the weight of box Y is less than the weight of box X.

D.text: Box Y gains more gravitational potential energy than box X as more work is done by the force acting on box Y than by the force acting on box X.
